## Demonstrated gaps and changes

- Initial commands stopped before tests because the shared Nix fetcher cache was full. A new task-owned XDG_CACHE_HOME allowed the same exact pinned shell to run; no shared cache was cleaned or global setting changed.
- Original actual local run failed ENOSPC while initializing /tmp/shop-reproducible-build and left its newly created zero-byte marker. Initial absence and terminal process were observed. Cleanup removed only that known new empty marker/directory; no unrelated/shared resource was removed. The helper now owns marker creation exclusively, tracks directory/file identity, cleans its own partial initialization and refuses changed markers/extra files. Existing targets are never adopted.
- An explicit `--canonical-build-root` may select only a new direct child of the checkout-owned .scratch. The legacy /tmp default remains. The chosen absolute path is recorded as a build input; these observations do not assert byte equivalence across different canonical paths. Both builds still use separate fresh roots/installs with the same process-visible input path in private mount/network namespaces, leaving the parent mount namespace unchanged.
- backend_package previously omitted every runtime template, stylesheet and catalog/document JSON. It now packages the same explicit runtime asset families as the qualified Nix application source plus Python/requirements. Both real builds include280 files: all276 exact application-source files and four requirement inputs. Runtime asset symlinks reject; private .env, unrelated JSON and HTML are excluded by the narrow source selection. Artifact source-byte identity is checked, not normalized after comparison.
- Record mode previously replaced two historical JSON files before validating. It now validates new candidate metadata before publishing only a new content-addressed revision with exclusive file creation/readback. A forced schema rejection proves old evidence remains unchanged and publishes no new JSON. No full aggregate marker is introduced.
